request.question: What would a 36-hour port outage at quarter end cost us?

answer:
A 36-hour port outage on the last vessel of Q1 FY2027 (VC-0127) would have cost **USD 17.7 M in lost EBITDA** plus USD 25,107 in demurrage, compared to zero financial impact from the *actual* 36-hour outage mid-quarter on VC-0115 (17 August).

**Comparison: Real vs. Quarter-End Outage (36 hours)**

| Scenario | Outage date | Vessel | Deferred tonnes | Deferred FOB revenue (USD) | Demurrage from outage (USD) | EBITDA change (USD) | Quarter | Source |
|----------|-------------|--------|-----------------|----------------------------|------------------------------|---------------------|---------|--------|
| **Actual** | 17 Aug 2026 | VC-0115 | 0 | 0 | 30,519 | 0 | Q1 FY2027 | MIXED (OPS, port, SAP_STANDIN, BillingDocument) |
| **What-if** | Quarter-end | VC-0127 | 177,700 | 19,143,621 | 25,107 | –17,707,849 | Q1 FY2027 | MIXED (OPS, port, SAP_STANDIN, BillingDocument) |

**Golden thread: signal → impact → action**  
The real 36-hour ship-loader failure (SL-01) on 17 August delayed VC-0115 by 36 hours and triggered USD 30,519 demurrage, but the vessel completed within the quarter. Had the same outage hit VC-0127 at quarter-end, 177,700 tonnes would slip into Q2, deferring USD 19.1 M revenue and cutting Q1 EBITDA by USD 17.7 M. The root cause was a 200KW motor stock-out (MZ-SP-A101, sole supplier 0017300001).

**Next step:** Establish dual-source supply or safety stock for the 200KW motor (MZ-SP-A101) and simulate loader redundancy to keep the last vessel of each quarter inside the reporting window.
